clue.text: Plays a biblical part

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: Plays are dramatic performances, and a book of the Bible is called the Acts of the Apostles.

clue.text: With a fabricated tale people can cause disaffection

parts.note: a made-up story is a lie
a people, as in a whole race or country, is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone with an invented story is able to turn the public against something.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement or disaffection is the feeling of being cut off and turned against others.

clue.text: His constructive work's topping!

parts.note: read as praise for a builder's splendid work, but literally a tradesman whose building job is putting the top covering on a roof

explanation.surface: Admiration for a builder whose work is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying slates or tiles literally tops off a building.

clue.text: Job producing cocoa put in jeopardy

indicators.note: putting the letters in jeopardy means putting them at risk of being knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A post whose duties could endanger a supply of cocoa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' looks like a phrase going with 'jeopardy', but both words are fodder: COCOA PUT IN is rearranged, signalled by 'jeopardy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's employment or trade is their line of work.

clue.text: Talk about a crazy fellow

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland, and the saying 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or prattle is a stream of light, rapid conversation.

clue.text: Don't exercise so much-it's futile

definitions.meaning: a piece of advice: employ it to a smaller degree, i.e. two words meaning employ to a smaller extent

explanation.definitionFit: Futile means pointless or ineffective, and the first part splits as a plea to employ something to a smaller degree.

clue.text: Gift for which there is a charge!

definitions.meaning: a prize or grant bestowed on someone

definitions.text: for which there is a charge!
definitions.meaning: a ward is a person in somebody's charge, such as a child under a guardian

explanation.definitionFit: A prize is something bestowed, and a ward is one placed in another's charge, so split as two words the answer fits too.

clue.text: Ruination following a wicked creature's threatening

indicators.note: the ruin word comes after, i.e. follows, the creature word

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
an ending is a finish or destruction

explanation.surface: Doom is approaching because of some evil being.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looming or about to happen is menacing, like an approaching storm.

clue.text: Invalid Greek character attended by inexperienced persons

parts.note: nu is the 13th letter of the Greek alphabet
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates; two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A Greek with no legal standing accompanied by novices.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract that is void has no legal force, and so is not valid.

clue.text: Totters off after a witness

indicators.note: the shuffled word is placed after the A
off suggests going wrong, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tottering person goes away after seeing something happen.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attests or vouches for something under oath bears witness.

clue.text: When out of sorts a kid gets one on edge

parts.note: feeling out of sorts is feeling unwell
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A grumpy child winds somebody up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and uncomfortable is being tense or on edge.

clue.text: Dismay at finding a mate without cash

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the friend phrase goes round the money

parts.note: a mate is a friend, a pal
P for penny or pence, a unit of British money

explanation.surface: Distress at discovering one's friend is broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify or shock someone is to fill them with dismay.

clue.text: She tends to hasten back to quarters

indicators.note: back means the word for hasten is read backwards

parts.note: to hasten is to run
S and E, south and east, are two quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying home to their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer tends the sick, so she is one who tends.

clue.text: Middle-men in commerce taking certain steps

indicators.note: in means the centre letter goes inside the business word

parts.note: commerce is trading

indicators.note: middle points to the central letter of the word men

explanation.surface: Intermediaries in business doing the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-men' looks like one word for agents, but it splits: the middle of 'men', E, goes in TRADING.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking means placing one's feet in steps, i.e. pacing over ground.

clue.text: A writer went on about the French and got through

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
et is French for and
rated in its old sense, scolded or berated someone at length

explanation.surface: An author lectured the French and made it through.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces do not come in clue order: the French word for 'and' sits between the writer and the scolding. 'Rated' is an old verb meaning to berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or pass into something is to get through it.

clue.text: Made to flower using heating equipment

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Forcing a plant to bloom by using a heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance that browns bread with heated elements is heating equipment.

clue.text: Pledge given by senator is broken

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are smashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A politician's promise is not kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm declaration or affirmation is a kind of pledge.

clue.text: Disease may be spread by water

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Illness can be transmitted through contaminated water.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast or beach is the area by the sea, by water.

clue.text: A police examination can be quite an ordeal

parts.note: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detectives
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Being questioned by detectives can be hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial that proves worth, like gold tested with nitric acid, is quite an ordeal.

clue.text: Notice to keep

definitions.meaning: to keep a law or festival is to honour or follow it

explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, and to honour a custom or rule is to keep it.

clue.text: Anti-irritant obtained from English trees

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
the ash is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy extracted from English woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion bathing the eyes soothes irritation, so it is an anti-irritant.

clue.text: Hair-style for the stony?

definitions.meaning: a short, tapered women's haircut of the 1920s
a beach of pebbles and small stones

explanation.definitionFit: A 1920s bobbed cut was so named, and pebbles on a beach make up stony ground.

clue.text: A Moslem lady takes little fruit

definitions.meaning: the wife, mother or daughter of a sultan

explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's wife bears the title, and a dried seedless grape has the same name.

clue.text: An old head of state will require credit order before spring

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A former leader needs a loan arranged before the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell was Lord Protector, ruling England in the 1650s.

clue.text: A story-teller of fifty into excavation

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the dig

parts.note: a mine is a dug excavation
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A narrator aged fifty goes down a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh tales.

clue.text: Judge coming from a Continental city

definitions.meaning: an ancient city in western Germany on the Moselle

explanation.definitionFit: One who tries cases judges them, and the German city on the Moselle shares the name.

clue.text: The best one to make business arrangements

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal is to trade or do business

explanation.surface: The optimal person for negotiating contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfection, the most desirable state, is the best one could hope for.

clue.text: Second-hand, but found serviceable

explanation.definitionFit: A pre-owned car is not new, and something put to work has been employed.

clue.text: Not stirring nevertheless

explanation.definitionFit: A motionless pond is calm, and the adverb meaning even so is a synonym of nevertheless.

clue.text: The gathering meant perhaps to hold a service

indicators.note: the reworked word holds the church service inside it
perhaps suggests the word could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Perhaps the congregation intended to hold a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the word into AMENT, and 'to hold' puts the church service inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection, or the act of heaping things up, is a gathering.

clue.text: A fool in the pool — if pushed under he admen-ishes no-one

indicators.note: in tells the solver the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A joke about a swimming-pool clown who, ducked, scolds no one.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'pusheD UNDER HE ADmen' holds the answer; the rest, including 'admen-ishes', a pun on admonishes, is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt or blockhead is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Cheerful note written by a boy

parts.note: G is a musical note
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A happy message written by a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling happy and pleased is being cheerful.
